title: Zeroing maxAmount while leaving a non-zero slope distinguishes a paused conduit from a retired one
content:
Three consecutive Aave Core instances are dormant but not identically so. Aave Core USDC (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.2.2.2.4.1) publishes inflow "`maxAmount`: 0, `slope`: 25,000,000 USDC per day"; Aave Core USDS (.2.3.2.4.1) is the same with USDS. Aave Core USDT (.2.4.2.4.1/.2) publishes "`maxAmount`: 0, `slope`: 0" on **both** legs.

Because `maxAmount` is the hard ceiling, all three are equally unable to move capital today. The difference is entirely in intent recorded through the second parameter. A zero ceiling with a live refill rate is a conduit whose sizing has already been agreed and only needs the ceiling raised; a double zero is a conduit with no agreed sizing at all.

This gives the parameter pair an expressive range the status taxonomy lacks. `Active` versus absent from the tree is binary; (`maxAmount`, `slope`) encodes at least three operational states — running, ceiling-suppressed, and fully zeroed — without any change to the document hierarchy or to governance status labels.

The cost is that this distinction is a convention readable only by comparing two numbers, and nothing in the documents states it. An operator or risk reviewer scanning `Active` instances has no labelled way to tell a temporarily suppressed venue from one that was zeroed and forgotten, which is exactly the kind of ambiguity that lets a stale configuration sit unexamined.
description: Aave Core USDC and USDS hold maxAmount 0 with a 25,000,000/day slope, while Aave Core USDT is zeroed on both parameters — two visibly different dormant states inside the same Active container.
